feedback.problem: Find the radius of the osculating circle at the point where $t=0$ for the curve $r(t)=⟨4{t}^{2},\,4t⟩.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $r(t)$, we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$, ${r}^{′}(0),$ and $‖{r}^{′}(0)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨8t,\,4⟩ \\  & =4⟨2t,\,1⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =4⟨2(0),\,1⟩ \\  & =4⟨0,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =4⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =4⟨2,\,0⟩ \\  & =8⟨1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(0) & =8⟨1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(0)$ and ${r}^{″}(0)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0) & =4⟨0,\,1,\,0⟩\times 8⟨1,\,0,\,0⟩ \\  & =32\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =32\,\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-32k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0)‖ & =32\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(0){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{{4}^{3}}{32} \\  & =\frac{64}{32} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
